Name: MongoDB
SDKs & notable repos: Official drivers for 12+ languages; Atlas Data API; Compass
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs downloadable per version; MongoDB University courses free
Notes: Document store with a mature query language. Read the replica-set election and write-concern docs — that is where the distributed-systems content lives.

Name: Apache Cassandra
Notes: The canonical Dynamo-style wide-column store. Tunable consistency makes the quorum maths concrete.

Name: ScyllaDB
Notes: C++ rewrite of Cassandra on a shard-per-core architecture. The Seastar design docs are excellent on thread-per-core.

Name: Redis
SDKs & notable repos: Clients in every language; Redis Stack modules
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs site; source is famously readable C
Notes: Read the source — `t_string.c`, `dict.c`, `ae.c` are a short course in systems C.

Name: Valkey
Notes: The Linux Foundation fork created after Redis's 2024 licence change. Now the default in several distributions.

Name: Amazon DynamoDB
SDKs & notable repos: AWS SDKs; DynamoDB Local for offline development
Notes: Read the original Dynamo paper and the 2022 USENIX ATC paper on the production system together.

Name: Apache HBase
Downloadable / offline docs: The HBase book as a single HTML page — also downloadable
Notes: The open Bigtable implementation. Read with the Bigtable paper.

Name: FoundationDB
SDKs & notable repos: Bindings for C, Python, Java, Go, Ruby
Notes: Strictly serializable distributed transactions, plus a deterministic simulation testing approach that is the most interesting part of the project.

Name: Neo4j
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs downloadable as PDF per manual
Notes: Cypher became the basis for the ISO GQL standard.

Name: ArangoDB
SDKs & notable repos: Multi-model: document, graph and key-value in one engine

Name: InfluxDB
Notes: Version 3 is a substantial rewrite on Arrow and DataFusion — check which version documentation you are reading.

Name: TimescaleDB
SDKs & notable repos: PostgreSQL extension — all PostgreSQL clients work
Notes: Now branded TigerData; the extension remains Timescale.

Name: Elasticsearch
Notes: Distributed search with a real sharding and replication model underneath.

Name: OpenSearch
Notes: The Apache 2.0 fork maintained after Elastic's licence change.

Name: etcd
SDKs & notable repos: gRPC API; clientv3 in Go and others
Notes: The Raft store behind Kubernetes. `etcd-io/raft` is a separate, very readable library.

Name: etcd Raft library
SDKs & notable repos: Production Raft as a standalone Go library
Notes: The best-documented production Raft implementation. Read it after the Raft paper.

Name: Apache ZooKeeper
SDKs & notable repos: Java and C clients; Curator recipes
Notes: ZAB rather than Raft. The recipes document (locks, barriers, leader election) is the practical part.

Name: HashiCorp Consul
SDKs & notable repos: HTTP API, DNS interface, service mesh

Name: hashicorp/raft
SDKs & notable repos: The other widely deployed Go Raft library
Notes: Compare with etcd's — the design differences are instructive.

Name: raft.github.io
SDKs & notable repos: The Raft homepage: paper, visualization, and a list of 100+ implementations
Notes: The interactive visualization teaches leader election faster than any text.

Name: Apache Kafka
Downloadable / offline docs: Single-page documentation — downloadable as one HTML file
Notes: The design section of the docs is a genuine distributed-systems paper. KRaft has replaced ZooKeeper.

Name: Apache Pulsar
SDKs & notable repos: Clients in many languages; BookKeeper underneath
Notes: Separates serving from storage. Worth studying as a contrast to Kafka's design.

Name: NATS
SDKs & notable repos: Clients in 40+ languages; JetStream for persistence
Notes: Small, fast, operationally simple. The server source is readable Go.

Name: RabbitMQ
Notes: The tutorials are the best introduction to messaging patterns generally.

Name: Apache Flink
SDKs & notable repos: DataStream and Table APIs; Java, Scala, Python
Notes: The checkpointing and exactly-once chapters are the valuable reading.

Name: Apache Beam
Notes: The Dataflow model paper behind it is the clearest treatment of event time and watermarks.

Name: Ray
SDKs & notable repos: Python-first distributed compute; Train, Tune, Serve
Notes: Also central to the ML ecosystem — see the ML/AI index.

Name: Temporal
SDKs & notable repos: SDKs for Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, .NET
Notes: Durable execution — the most interesting recent idea in distributed application design.

Name: Jepsen
SDKs & notable repos: Clojure testing framework; the analyses are the real artefact
Notes: Kyle Kingsbury's reports on real databases under partition. Read three of them and your trust calibration changes permanently.

Name: Maelstrom
SDKs & notable repos: A workbench for writing toy distributed systems and having them tested properly
Downloadable / offline docs: In-repo docs and a full tutorial
Notes: The best hands-on way to learn distributed systems. Start here, not with a book.

Name: Gossip Glomers (fly.io)
SDKs & notable repos: A guided challenge series built on Maelstrom: broadcast, CRDTs, Kafka-style logs, transactions
Notes: Probably the single best free practical distributed-systems course. Six challenge sets, real verification.

Name: TLA+
SDKs & notable repos: TLA+ Toolbox, TLC model checker, PlusCal
Downloadable / offline docs: Lamport's video course and the Hyperbook, both free
Notes: Used at AWS and Microsoft to find real protocol bugs before implementation.

Name: Learn TLA+
SDKs & notable repos: A much gentler entry point than Lamport's own materials
Notes: Start here if TLA+ has bounced off you before.

Name: Raft paper
Notes: Read this before any consensus implementation. It was written to be understandable, and it is.

Name: Paxos Made Simple
SDKs & notable repos: Lamport's attempt at an accessible Paxos explanation
Notes: Still harder than Raft. Read it second, for the lineage.

Name: Lamport's publications
SDKs & notable repos: Time/Clocks, Byzantine Generals, Paxos — with retrospective commentary on each
Notes: The commentary explaining why each paper was written is as useful as the papers.

Name: crdt.tech
SDKs & notable repos: The CRDT reference: papers, implementations, talks
Notes: Start here for conflict-free replicated data types rather than with a single library.

Name: Distributed Systems (van Steen & Tanenbaum)
Notes: A proper textbook, legitimately free.

Name: awesome-distributed-systems
SDKs & notable repos: Curated papers, books, talks and systems

Name: dancres/Pages
SDKs & notable repos: A large annotated reading list of distributed-systems papers
Notes: One of the best-curated paper lists available.

Name: TigerBeetle
SDKs & notable repos: Financial accounting database in Zig; Viewstamped Replication consensus; deterministic simulation testing
Notes: The most rigorous open testing methodology currently shipping. The simulator and the design docs are the reason to read it.

Name: Automerge
SDKs & notable repos: CRDT library for local-first applications; Rust core with JS and Swift bindings
Notes: The most approachable production CRDT implementation. Read with crdt.tech.

Name: Yjs
Notes: Powers a lot of real collaborative software. Benchmarks and internals are documented openly.

Name: Apache BookKeeper
SDKs & notable repos: Replicated log storage; the durability layer under Pulsar
Notes: A distributed write-ahead log as a standalone service. Useful to study separately from Pulsar.

Name: Dapr
SDKs & notable repos: Portable building blocks for distributed applications: state, pub/sub, bindings, actors
Notes: An opinionated abstraction over the patterns. Read the component model before adopting it.

Name: Hazelcast
SDKs & notable repos: In-memory data grid with distributed data structures and CP subsystem
Notes: The CP subsystem is a Raft implementation worth reading alongside etcd’s.

Name: Chaos Mesh
SDKs & notable repos: Kubernetes-native fault injection: network partitions, latency, pod kills
Notes: The practical way to apply Jepsen-style thinking to your own cluster.

Name: LitmusChaos
SDKs & notable repos: CNCF chaos engineering framework with a public experiment hub

Name: arXiv
SDKs & notable repos: Preprints across all of CS; most systems, ML and PL work appears here before publication
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper is a free PDF. Bulk access documented at https://info.arxiv.org/help/bulk_data/index.html; a full-text API at export.arxiv.org
Notes: Not peer-reviewed. Treat an arXiv-only paper as a claim, not a result — but it is where you will read almost everything first.

Name: ar5iv
SDKs & notable repos: Renders any arXiv paper as responsive HTML instead of PDF
Notes: Makes papers readable on a phone and searchable in-page. Underused.

Name: alphaXiv
SDKs & notable repos: arXiv papers with a public comment and discussion layer
Notes: Useful when a paper is contested — the discussion often contains the critique you were looking for.

Name: Semantic Scholar
SDKs & notable repos: 200M+ papers with citation graph, influential-citation scoring and TLDR summaries
Downloadable / offline docs: Free Graph API (https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api), bulk datasets available on request
Notes: The best free citation graph. 'Highly influential citations' is a genuinely useful filter for finding what actually mattered.

Name: OpenAlex
SDKs & notable repos: Fully open catalogue of works, authors, venues and institutions; successor to Microsoft Academic Graph
Downloadable / offline docs: Entirely free API with no key required; complete database snapshots downloadable
Notes: The only large-scale bibliographic database that is open all the way down, including bulk snapshots.

Name: DBLP
SDKs & notable repos: Authoritative CS bibliography — complete author and venue listings
Notes: The fastest way to find everything a given researcher has published, and to see a conference's full programme by year.

Name: OpenReview
SDKs & notable repos: ICLR, NeurIPS, COLM and dozens of other venues — papers plus the full review threads
Notes: Reading the reviews and author rebuttals teaches you how the field evaluates work. Nothing else exposes this.

Name: CORE
SDKs & notable repos: Aggregates 300M+ open-access papers from repositories worldwide
Notes: Good for finding the green open-access copy when a publisher's version is paywalled.

Name: Unpaywall
SDKs & notable repos: Finds legal free copies of paywalled papers via DOI
Notes: Legal, author-deposited copies only. Install the extension and most paywalls simply stop appearing.

Name: Papers We Love
SDKs & notable repos: A curated, categorised repository of classic CS papers with local meetup talks
Downloadable / offline docs: Repo cloneable; many PDFs mirrored in-repo
Notes: The best starting point if you do not yet know which papers matter in a subfield.

Name: The Morning Paper (archive)
Notes: No longer updated, but the back catalogue of ~1000 summarised papers is one of the great free CS resources.

Name: USENIX Proceedings
SDKs & notable repos: OSDI, SOSP (co-published), NSDI, ATC, FAST, Security — the core systems venues
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper free, immediately, with no membership. Often with recorded talks
Notes: USENIX made everything open access years before the rest of the field. If a systems paper exists, check here first.

Name: ACM Digital Library
SDKs & notable repos: SIGMOD, ASPLOS, PLDI, POPL, SoCC and the ACM journals
Downloadable / offline docs: Partly open: ACM Open and author-paid OA papers are free; others are paywalled
Notes: 403s to automated clients; loads in a browser. For paywalled items, check arXiv, the author's homepage or Unpaywall first — the free copy usually exists.

Name: IEEE Xplore
SDKs & notable repos: ISCA, MICRO, HPCA and the IEEE journals
Notes: Almost always worth searching the author's page or arXiv instead. Architecture authors in particular post preprints widely.

Name: DROPS / LIPIcs (Dagstuhl)
SDKs & notable repos: ECOOP, ITP, CONCUR, SAT and many theory venues
Downloadable / offline docs: 100% open access, free PDFs, Creative Commons licensed
Notes: A fully open publisher. Every paper, always free, no exceptions.

Name: arXiv cs.DC (Distributed Computing)
SDKs & notable repos: Distributed, parallel and cluster computing preprints

Name: USENIX NSDI
Notes: Where most large-scale distributed infrastructure work is published.

Name: USENIX OSDI
SDKs & notable repos: Systems and distributed systems, free and open
Notes: Raft, Spanner-adjacent work and most consensus systems research lands here or at SOSP.

Name: PODC
SDKs & notable repos: Principles of Distributed Computing — the theory side
Downloadable / offline docs: Via ACM DL; most authors post preprints
Notes: This is where impossibility results and lower bounds live. Harder reading, but foundational.

Name: DISC
Notes: Fully open access through Dagstuhl. Theory-focused.

Name: The Paper Trail
SDKs & notable repos: Henry Robinson's distributed systems writing, including the classic consensus explainers
Notes: The 'Paxos made abstract' material is clearer than most formal treatments.

Name: Metadata (Murat Demirbas)
SDKs & notable repos: Long-running paper review blog from a distributed systems researcher
Notes: Reviews of both classic and current papers, with honest criticism.

Name: Jepsen analyses
SDKs & notable repos: Empirical consistency testing reports on real databases
Notes: Not peer-reviewed and more consequential than most papers that are.

Name: Gossip Glomers
Notes: Six challenge sets — unique IDs, broadcast, CRDT counters, a Kafka-style log, distributed transactions — each verified by a real checker. Free. Do this before any textbook.

Name: Maelstrom
Notes: The workbench underneath Gossip Glomers. Write a node in any language; it injects partitions and checks linearizability.

Name: MIT 6.824 / 6.5840 Distributed Systems
Notes: Labs where you implement MapReduce, Raft, a fault-tolerant KV store and sharding — in Go, with public tests. The best university course in the field, entirely free.

Name: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
Notes: Kleppmann's book is the common vocabulary of the field. Chapters 5-9 are the heart of it.

Name: Distributed Systems, 4th edition
Notes: A free, complete textbook if you want formal treatment alongside DDIA.

Name: Raft paper
Notes: Deliberately written to be understandable. Read it once properly and consensus stops being mysterious.

Name: raft.github.io visualization
Notes: Watch leader election and log replication happen. Ten minutes well spent before the paper.

Name: Jepsen analyses
Notes: Real databases, real partitions, documented failures. Read the Cassandra, MongoDB and etcd reports.

Name: Jepsen framework
Notes: How the testing actually works.

Name: Fallacies of distributed computing
Notes: Eight assumptions that are always wrong. Short, and worth revisiting periodically.

Name: etcd
SDKs & notable repos: First systems to run and read
Notes: A small, real, Raft-backed store you can run locally and inspect.

Name: Redis
SDKs & notable repos: First systems to run and read
Notes: Readable C, clear docs, and the clustering model is a good first look at sharding.

Name: NATS
SDKs & notable repos: First systems to run and read
Notes: Simplest serious messaging system to get running.

Name: RabbitMQ tutorials
SDKs & notable repos: First systems to run and read
Notes: The six tutorials cover messaging patterns better than most books.

Name: Apache Kafka documentation
SDKs & notable repos: First systems to run and read
Notes: Read the 'Design' section specifically — it is effectively a paper.

Name: Lamport's publications
Notes: Start with 'Time, Clocks and the Ordering of Events'. Short, and foundational to everything after.

Name: Kleppmann's Cambridge lecture notes
Notes: A complete free course text, more formal than DDIA and much shorter than a textbook.

Name: crdt.tech
Notes: The entry point for eventual consistency done properly.

Name: Papers We Love
Notes: Start here when you do not yet know which papers matter. Curated by subfield, with recorded talks.

Name: The Morning Paper archive
Notes: Around a thousand papers summarised in plain language. No longer updated; still one of the best free CS resources.

Name: Semantic Scholar
Notes: Free citation graph. The 'highly influential citations' filter is the fastest way to find what a paper actually changed.

Name: Unpaywall
Notes: Install the extension. Most paywalls stop appearing, legally, because the author deposited a copy.

Name: ar5iv
Notes: Read any arXiv paper as HTML instead of a two-column PDF. Swap arxiv.org/abs for ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html.

Name: MIT 6.824 Raft labs
Notes: Lab 2 is Raft from scratch against an adversarial test suite. Difficult and worth it.

Name: etcd Raft library
Notes: Read this after your own implementation works. The gap is educational.

Name: hashicorp/raft
Notes: A second production implementation with different design choices.

Name: braft
Notes: Industrial C++ Raft, for a third perspective.

Name: Raft extended paper
Notes: Return to sections 5-8 once you have implementation scars.

Name: Paxos Made Simple
Notes: Understand the lineage Raft reacted against.

Name: TLA+
Notes: Specify your protocol and let the model checker find the interleaving you missed.

Name: Learn TLA+
Notes: The practical on-ramp. Start here, then go to Lamport's materials.

Name: TLA+ tools
Notes: TLC, the Toolbox, and the standard modules.

Name: Jepsen
Notes: Empirical verification as the complement to formal specification.

Name: FoundationDB
Notes: Deterministic simulation testing — arguably the most rigorous testing approach in any open database.

Name: Cassandra source
Notes: Dynamo-style replication, gossip and hinted handoff in a mature codebase.

Name: ScyllaDB
Notes: The same model rebuilt shard-per-core on Seastar. Read the Seastar design notes.

Name: Kafka
Notes: KRaft replaced ZooKeeper; read the KIPs for the migration reasoning.

Name: Pulsar
Notes: Storage and serving separated via BookKeeper. A deliberate contrast to Kafka.

Name: FoundationDB docs
Notes: Strictly serializable transactions over a distributed store, documented honestly about limits.

Name: MongoDB source
Notes: Replica set elections and the write-concern machinery.

Name: Apache Flink
Notes: The checkpointing and exactly-once semantics chapters are the real material.

Name: Apache Beam
Notes: Event time, watermarks and triggers, formalized.

Name: Temporal
Notes: Durable execution — read the architecture docs, not just the SDK tutorials.

Name: Ray
Notes: Distributed compute with a task and actor model; readable architecture docs.

Name: Apache Spark
Notes: Shuffle, lineage and recovery.

Name: Kleppmann's Cambridge notes
Notes: Precise definitions of the consistency models that blog posts blur together.

Name: crdt.tech
Notes: The research index for CRDTs and their implementations.

Name: Lamport publications
Notes: Byzantine Generals and the sequential consistency papers.

Name: dancres/Pages
Notes: An annotated paper list organised by topic — use it to plan reading.

Name: awesome-distributed-systems
Notes: Broader index including talks and books.

Name: PingCAP talent-plan
Notes: Structured courses building a distributed KV store in Rust and Go.

Name: USENIX OSDI
Notes: Free papers, and the main venue for systems work.

Name: ACM SOSP
Notes: Alternates with OSDI.

Notes: The theory half distributed systems courses skip: consensus, failure detectors, snapshot algorithms.

Notes: Where the networking half of distributed systems lands.

Notes: Proceedings plus selected recordings.

Notes: For the data-side papers (Spanner, Calvin, etc.), fully open.

Notes: Distributed systems, messaging and observability devrooms.

Notes: Distributed-infrastructure and federation tracks.
